claims.explanation: PD-123319 is an AT2 receptor (AGTR2) antagonist, and its selective cytotoxicity likely depends on AGTR2 expression, which is known to mediate nitric oxide/cGMP signaling and can promote apoptosis. The pattern of sensitive lines is enriched for TP53 mutations and RAS/MAPK pathway activation, suggesting that cells with defective p53 and high AGTR2 expression are more vulnerable to AT2 blockade. Conversely, lines with intact p53 or low AGTR2 expression are relatively resistant.

features.basis: AT2 receptor is the direct target of PD-123319; its expression is required for drug activity.
TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines, suggesting loss of p53-mediated apoptosis allows AT2 blockade to trigger alternative death pathways.
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines (LOVO, OV7, SNU81, TCCPAN2, PATU8988S), possibly linking RAS/MAPK-driven proliferation to AT2 signaling.
BRAF mutations are present in sensitive melanoma and other lines (UACC62, 22RV1), suggesting MAPK activation may enhance sensitivity.
ARID1A mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (LOVO, 22RV1, COLO792, MHHNB11), potentially altering chromatin and stress responses.
PTEN mutations are seen in sensitive lines (UACC62, SNU81), possibly via PI3K/AKT activation.
PIK3CA mutations occur in sensitive lines (22RV1, RT112), suggesting PI3K pathway activation may contribute.
STK11 mutations are found in sensitive lines (22RV1, EKVX, PLCPRF5), possibly linking metabolic stress to AT2 blockade.
CDKN2A mutations are more common in resistant lines (HS939T, SNU1214, HS766T, NCIH1915, LXF289), suggesting intact cell cycle checkpoints may mediate resistance.
CTNNB1 mutations appear in resistant lines (U2OS, HEC265, LXF289, SW480), possibly indicating Wnt activation confers resistance.
NFE2L2 mutations are present in resistant lines (SNUC5, HEC265, TE6), suggesting antioxidant response may protect against AT2-mediated oxidative stress.
ATM mutation in resistant line SNUC5 may indicate DNA damage response defects that reduce sensitivity.
